methods.label: Use the signs of the inner expressions
methods.explanation: Since \(a-1>0\) and \(a-3<0\), the original expression equals \((a-1)+(3-a)=2\).
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 square-root properties and Grade 7 sign reasoning, absolute values, and polynomial simplification.

methods.label: Interpret the terms as distances
methods.explanation: Using \(\sqrt{x^2}=|x|\), the two terms are the distances from \(a\) to \(1\) and from \(a\) to \(3\) on the number line. Since \(1<a<3\), these distances are the lengths of two adjacent segments that together form the segment from \(1\) to \(3\). Their sum is therefore \(3-1=2\), so the constant is \(2\).
methods.levelReason: Combines the same Grade 8 square-root identity with Grade 7 number-line distances and segment addition.
